1	# ReachyMini — Agent Instructions
2	
3	Native Swift client (macOS/iPadOS/iOS) for the Reachy Mini Wireless robot. Pure network client to the robot daemon's
4	HTTP/WebSocket API. Swift 6, strict concurrency.
5	
6	## Environment Setup — MANDATORY
7	
8	The development environment is installed **only** via:
9	
10	```bash
11	./bootstrap.sh
12	```
13	
14	It installs all pinned tools (swiftformat, swiftlint, hk, dprint, actionlint, git-cliff, xcsift, tuist) through the
15	self-contained `./bin/mise` binary and wires git hooks (`core.hooksPath .githooks`).
16	
17	- **Never** install tools globally (`brew install swiftlint`, `npm i -g`, etc.).
18	- **Never** call tools bare (`swift build`, `swiftlint`) — always `./bin/mise run <task>` or `./bin/mise x -- <tool>`,
19	  which guarantees pinned versions and PATH.
20	- Swift itself is managed by swiftly via `.swift-version`, not by mise.
21	- Tool versions are pinned in `mise.toml` + `mise.lock`. After editing `[tools]`: `trash mise.lock && ./bin/mise lock`.
22	  Find updates with `./bin/mise latest <tool>` — `mise outdated` reports nothing here, because an exact pin always
23	  matches its own request.
24	- The `hk` version in `mise.toml` must match the `hk@X.Y.Z` package URI in `hk.pkl` (bump together).
25	- `mise run project` (tuist generate) needs a one-time `./bin/mise x -- tuist auth login` — the project is connected
26	  to tuist.dev (`alexey1312/reachy-mini-desktop-app-swift` in `Apps/Tuist.swift`). That handle names the **tuist.dev
27	  project**, not this repository, and deliberately keeps the pre-rename name: renaming the GitHub repo does not rename
28	  the server-side project, so "fixing" it to match `reachy-mini-swift` points generation at a project that does not exist.
29	- Run every `tuist` command from `Apps/` — `Tuist.swift` lives there and tuist only searches _upward_, so from the repo
30	  root it finds no manifest and reports the project as unconnected to the server (`run 'tuist init'`).
31	- Use `mise run inspect:bundle [path]` rather than `tuist inspect bundle`: it handles the cwd, defaults to the iOS
32	  device bundle, and rejects a macOS one (which keeps `Info.plist` under `Contents/`, where the command wants it at
33	  the root). Size numbers only mean something off a Release archive — a Debug bundle carries `__preview.dylib`,
34	  `*.debug.dylib` and the provisioning profile, none of which ship.
35	- Do **not** set `enableCaching` — without a running cache daemon every compile task waits out a CAS socket deadline,
36	  and CI has neither the daemon nor cache credentials (this repo is not connected to the tuist.dev project).
37	- `Package.resolved` **oscillates between the two build systems, and neither is wrong.** `xcodebuild` resolves the
38	  whole Tuist workspace and writes back to the root package's file, adding five pins (Prefire, swift-snapshot-testing,
39	  swift-syntax, swift-custom-dump, xctest-dynamic-overlay); `swift build` / `swift test` see only the root package and
40	  strip them again. Merging a branch that predates them drops them silently too — git sees a clean delete on one side.
41	  Commit the 16-pin version (run `mise run project` or any snapshot task last), never hand-edit it, and expect the
42	  file to show as modified after a plain `mise run test`.
43	
44	## Quick Reference
45	
46	```bash
47	./bin/mise run build          # Debug build (piped through xcsift)
48	./bin/mise run build:app      # Build the ReachySpike app target (generates first)
49	./bin/mise run test           # All tests, parallel
50	./bin/mise run test:filter T  # Filter tests
51	./bin/mise run lint           # SwiftLint --strict + actionlint + hk lockstep
52	./bin/mise run format         # Format all (hk fix --all)
53	./bin/mise run format-check   # CI formatting check
54	./bin/mise run project        # tuist generate (Apps/)
55	./bin/mise run inspect:bundle # Upload an iOS bundle-size analysis to tuist.dev
56	./bin/mise run sim-daemon     # Simulated robot daemon (MuJoCo, LAN-reachable)
57	./bin/mise run test:sim       # Integration tests against a running sim-daemon
58	./bin/mise run update-spec    # Refresh + normalize daemon OpenAPI spec
59	./bin/mise run test:snapshots # Snapshot-test every ReachyUI preview (iOS Simulator)
60	./bin/mise run test:snapshots:record  # Re-record the reference images
61	./bin/mise run storybook      # Browsable catalogue of every preview, on a simulator
62	```
63	
64	`build` / `test` are SwiftPM only — they never compile `Apps/ReachySpike`. Use `build:app` for that; CI runs it as a
65	separate job, so app-target breakage no longer reaches `main` unnoticed.
66	`test:filter` matches type names (`RobotSessionAudioTests`), not `@Suite` display names.
67	`SimulatorIntegrationTests` is gated on `REACHY_SIM_HOST`, so plain `test` **skips it silently and reports green** —
68	run `test:sim` against a live `sim-daemon` to exercise it.
69	`swift test --skip-build` runs the previously built binary: rebuild with `swift build --build-tests` after editing a
70	test, or the run silently verifies stale code.
71	Everything pipes through xcsift, which on long runs can truncate and report `status: incomplete` while hiding the real
72	result — verify the artifact, or rerun the tool directly
73	(`./bin/mise x -- swiftlint lint --strict Sources Tests Apps/ReachySpike`). Always pass those explicit paths — a bare
74	`.` walks into `Apps/DerivedData`, and swiftformat then "fails" on generated and vendored sources.
75	`mise run clean` only clears `.build` — `Apps/DerivedData` (Xcode's, several GB) is not touched.
76	**SwiftPM holds one `.build` lock per worktree**, so a second invocation waits instead of failing, printing
77	`Another instance of SwiftPM (PID: …) is already running` — a line that never appears when the output is piped
78	through `tail`. A run that timed out in your tool keeps running and keeps the lock, and every later command then
79	looks like the code under test is hanging. Check `pgrep -f 'swift-build|swift-test|swift-frontend'` before
80	diagnosing a hang, and run one SwiftPM process at a time.
81	**A hang with no test output at all is the compiler, not the code.** `ps -o command= -p <frontend-pid>` names the
82	`-primary-file` it is stuck on and `sample <pid>` names the pass. One shape found here: a closure nested inside an
83	`AsyncStream { continuation in … }` builder that captures the escaping continuation (e.g. `lock.withLock { … }`
84	assigning it to a stored property) emits a `convert_escape_to_noescape` that sends the `ClosureLifetimeFixup` SIL
85	pass into a dominator walk it does not return from — 20+ minutes of one core, no diagnostic, no timeout. It is a
86	diagnostic pass, so `-Onone` does not avoid it; flatten the nesting and lock by hand instead
87	(`Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift` carries the worked example).
88	Two files sharing a basename in one target fail as `couldn't build <name>.swift.o because of multiple producers`,
89	never as a redeclaration and never naming the other file — check `find Sources -name Foo.swift` before adding one.
90	`sim-daemon` **cannot** serve `/wifi/*` or `/update/*`: `--wireless-version` crashes on import (`.venv-sim` has
91	neither `nmcli` nor `cryptography`), and `main.py` would run robot-image maintenance on your Mac. Those routes are
92	covered by `StubURLProtocol` / `LocalWebSocketServer` and real hardware only. BLE likewise — the robot's GATT service

# ReachyKit

Transport + domain core. No UI imports (SwiftUI/UIKit forbidden here). Swift 6 strict concurrency.

- `openapi.json` + `openapi-generator-config.yaml` → client generated at build time by the OpenAPIGenerator plugin
  (types + client, idiomatic naming). Refresh spec: `./bin/mise run update-spec` (fetches + normalizes null-type
  anyOf branches the generator can't handle — see `Scripts/normalize-openapi.py`).
- Pydantic `Optional[X]` without a default is _required and nullable_; the normalizer must also drop such properties
  from `required`, or the generated Swift field is non-Optional and a real null throws (`DaemonStatus.backend_status`).
- WebSocket endpoints are hand-written (not in the spec) — see `Transport/`.
- Unknown JSON fields must never break decoding (daemon updates independently of this app).
- `RobotAPIClient` supplies throwing defaults for everything except `handshake`, `daemonStatus`, `wakeUp` and
  `gotoSleep` — every test double must implement those four. `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` live on separate protocols so
  doubles for the connection surface stay small.
- Bluetooth layers as `BLETransport` (CoreBluetooth behind a seam; `FakeBLETransport` is the only stand-in, since the
  robot's GATT service is Linux/BlueZ) → `BLECommandPump` (one command at a time, write→read→maybe-notify) →
  `BLELink` (`@MainActor @Observable`, the screens' state). One link per transport: the response characteristic
  carries no correlation id, so a second pump on the same transport would race the first for its replies. Provisioning
  and recovery are therefore two halves of `BLELink`, not two session types (`BLELink+Recovery.swift`).
- Provisioning is written against `WiFiProvisioningTransport`, not against BLE: `BLEProvisioningTransport` and
  `RobotConnection` both implement it, so the sealing and the screens are shared and the HTTP path is available if the
  ~260-byte sealed payload turns out not to fit one ATT write. `WiFiConfigClient` adds the settings-only routes.
- `BLECommand` is the whole set the robot answers — anything else comes back as `ECHO:`. Renaming is **not** in it:
  daemon 1.9.0's dispatch has no `SET_NAME` branch, and it does not mount `POST /api/daemon/robot-name` either — that
  route postdates the release, so on 1.9.0 a robot cannot be renamed at all. `handshake` probes the route and reports
  `supportsRename`; the field is greyed out rather than left to 404 on save.

# ReachyKit

Transport + domain core. No UI imports (SwiftUI/UIKit forbidden here). Swift 6 strict concurrency.

- `openapi.json` + `openapi-generator-config.yaml` → client generated at build time by the OpenAPIGenerator plugin
  (types + client, idiomatic naming). Refresh spec: `./bin/mise run update-spec` (fetches + normalizes null-type
  anyOf branches the generator can't handle — see `Scripts/normalize-openapi.py`).
- Pydantic `Optional[X]` without a default is _required and nullable_; the normalizer must also drop such properties
  from `required`, or the generated Swift field is non-Optional and a real null throws (`DaemonStatus.backend_status`).
- WebSocket endpoints are hand-written (not in the spec) — see `Transport/`.
- Unknown JSON fields must never break decoding (daemon updates independently of this app).
- `RobotAPIClient` supplies throwing defaults for everything except `handshake`, `daemonStatus`, `wakeUp` and
  `gotoSleep` — every test double must implement those four. `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` live on separate protocols so
  doubles for the connection surface stay small.
- Bluetooth layers as `BLETransport` (CoreBluetooth behind a seam; `FakeBLETransport` is the only stand-in, since the
  robot's GATT service is Linux/BlueZ) → `BLECommandPump` (one command at a time, write→read→maybe-notify) →
  `BLELink` (`@MainActor @Observable`, the screens' state). One link per transport: the response characteristic
  carries no correlation id, so a second pump on the same transport would race the first for its replies. Provisioning
  and recovery are therefore two halves of `BLELink`, not two session types (`BLELink+Recovery.swift`).
- Provisioning is written against `WiFiProvisioningTransport`, not against BLE: `BLEProvisioningTransport` and
  `RobotConnection` both implement it, so the sealing and the screens are shared and the HTTP path is available if the
  ~260-byte sealed payload turns out not to fit one ATT write. `WiFiConfigClient` adds the settings-only routes.
- `RemoteDataChannel` is the seam under a remote session, and the **end of `messages()` is terminal**:
  `RemoteControlChannel` reads it as "the session is over" and fails every waiter with `.closed`. A peer being
  replaced must therefore not end it — every WebRTC negotiation replaces the peer, the _first offer included_, so
  conflating the two broke remote control on the very first handshake and left the reader deaf for good (it now
  re-subscribes, `endReading`). `WebRTCDataChannel` splits the two: `detachPeer()` is a gap (sends go back to
  waiting, the stream lives), `close()` is an ending. `isOpen` exists for the same distinction one layer up — a
  command issued while the channel is between peers is timing a negotiation, not a robot, and gets `openingTimeout`
  (30 s) rather than the reply budget (10 s). Ask it afresh; the opening wait comes back after every ICE failure.
- `BLECommand` is the whole set the robot answers — anything else comes back as `ECHO:`. Renaming is **not** in it:
  daemon 1.9.0's dispatch has no `SET_NAME` branch, and it does not mount `POST /api/daemon/robot-name` either — that
  route postdates the release, so on 1.9.0 a robot cannot be renamed at all. `handshake` probes the route and reports
  `supportsRename`; the field is greyed out rather than left to 404 on save.

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's

and `close()` is an ending, reached only from `stop()`, a failure, and a
session end that names a reason. That is the same line `phase` was
already drawn on. The reader clears itself when the stream does end, so
the next command asks for a new one.

A command issued while the channel is between peers is timing a
negotiation rather than a robot, so it gets its own `openingTimeout` of
30 s instead of the reply budget. Asked afresh through the new
`RemoteDataChannel.isOpen` rather than latched, because that wait comes
back after every ICE failure.

Both budgets end in `.timedOut`, so the tests assert the elapsed span as
well as the error — the wrong branch throws the same thing, just later.
